source.author: PingYou Ltd
source.method: Finite whole-owner directed face-port reconstruction, followed by exact rational decoding.
source.attribution_note: PingYou Ltd constructed the finite marked boundary return. The initial infinite cuboctahedral lattice is classical (Hoylman 1970), reported by Betke and Henk, Densest Lattice Packings of 3-Polytopes, Section 5. No claim of inventing that infinite lattice.

construction.name: finite_cuboctahedron_face_return
construction.coordinate_convention: Centers and canonical vertices multiplied by sqrt(2); owner support is 1 for coordinate normals and 2 for diagonal normals. Native unit-edge vertices are permutations of (0,+-1,+-1)/sqrt(2).
construction.physical_operation: Select whole owners in the classical cuboctahedral lattice at the declared host mark. Retain one actual directed face-separator per owner pair. Reconstruct all owner translations jointly from those ports and every finite host wall. A continued step reassigns ports to realized separating faces before reconstructing the whole state. A boundary exchange retires a wall controller and inserts one whole owner at a retained owner contact port, then solves the common completion retaining every other pair port. No owner is clipped; all intrinsic frames remain fixed.
construction.native_clearance: Dilate every exact owner center by 1+1/500000 and use host scale=(1+1/500000)*exact_nominal+1/500000; retain each unit owner.
construction.construction_change: Owner translations change nonuniformly relative to the source lattice indices. This is a new finite packing, not source-certificate padding or a common recentering.

Complete host faces, pair separators and common boundary closures are retained. Classical lattice sources are credited in every applicable record. The archive retains complete native coordinates, explicit physical construction decoders, original source and donor credits, independent geometry and construction reviews, and SHA256 manifests. All 32 witnesses pass the unmodified upstream floating checker and exact certifier.
